```{r}
#| include: false
library(apaTables)
```

HTML width rules. Two tables in one document: one apaTables builds, and one
the READER built themselves. The width rules apaTables added to `apa.css` are
scoped to a wrapper the package puts on its own tables, and the whole point of
that scoping is this document -- one of those rules overrides a table's column
proportions, and a table someone else wrote may carry proportions they chose
on purpose. So exactly one of the two tables below may come out wrapped.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ours
#| echo: false
apa.quarto.html(apa.cor.table(attitude[, 1:3]))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-theirs
#| tbl-cap: "A table the reader built"
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(head(attitude[, 1:2]), col.names = c("rating", "complaints"))
```

Body text after.
